Or are there meant to be? Just listening to Lúnasa, it kind of throws me off…

↳ Posted by Joe CSS on May 31st, 2008.

I’m trying to figure that out, looking at Lunasa’s first book while listening to it… it sounds like there’s something odd with it… Great tune, either way, though.

↳ Posted by Joseph Chordmichael on November 19th, 2008.

This tune is originally a crooked Quebecois tune, so it is not even measured. There is a even version out there which is sometimes played for contra dances.

↳ Posted by homebrewz on April 4th, 2010.

2 extra beats?

Most ‘crooked’ tunes i’ve run into seem to have an extra bar tacked on somewhere- this one has, as near as i can tell, an extra two beats. You can make them go away with a minimum of effort.

Song of Songs 7:12-13

↳ Posted by Damien Rogeau on January 12th, 2020.

Fleur De Mandragore, X:9

This one is transposed to D (just so it’s easier for whistles and flutes, etc.). It’s building off of X:8’s version, but a change in measure 9 and 10 of X:8 with the
2 ~B3d cA|AB ABce||
part. It’s condensed into one measure with the build up of measure 10 in X:8 being the last 2 beats in measure 9 in this version. (2 ~A3c GABd ). Hopefully that makes sense.
It’s also got some ornamentation for whistles and flutes in the B part of the tune.

↳ Posted by Dais on April 7th, 2025.
